The '''Jailor's Holocron''' housed the [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] of a [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], gentle and composed, his form woven from [[Color/Legends|white]] light. [[Gender/Legends|He]] had been created to oversee the healing of Jedi who strayed from the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]] and to guide them back to serenity. Unlike the [[Warden (Dawn Temple)|Warden]] or the [[Curator (Dawn Temple)|Curator]], the Jailor held full authority over the [[Dawn Temple]]'s systems, able to grant or deny access to its deepest chambers. Yet his power was tempered by compassion, for he judged not with severity but with mercy, offering counsel and redemption to all who sought it.<ref name="Lure of the Lost" />

After the fall of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the Jailor remained the senior gatekeeper of the Dawn Temple. He endured in silence, locked away from those he was meant to aid, still holding the wisdom of the archives and the key to the Temple's true purpose. To any who came before him, he asked not for flawless virtue but for sincerity of intent. Though the halls of the Temple crumbled and darkness pressed close, the Jailor waited with patience, guarding hope that the lost could yet be restored.<ref name="Lure of the Lost" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Jailor's Holocron first appeared in ''[[Lure of the Lost]]'', a downloadable adventure for [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' [[2015]] ''[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny]]'' [[Star Wars Roleplaying|roleplaying game]].
